source.title: Training BatchNorm and Only BatchNorm: On the Expressive Power of Random Features in CNNs
source.authors: Jonathan Frankle; D. Schwab; Ari S. Morcos

record.tranche_reason: The study trains BatchNorm affine parameters over frozen random features and reports test accuracy, but does not measure the training classification error or any other outcome named by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported accuracy results concern test accuracy for networks with most weights frozen, not training error under the claim's training recipes. The paper also discusses prior work on BatchNorm optimization, but those cited results are not its own.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual connections and BatchNorm to investigate affine-parameter expressivity. Section 3 explicitly selects ResNets because depth can increase without interfering with optimization. Its own results measure final test accuracy and feature sparsity, not the training-error, convergence-speed, or stability effects named by V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: affine parameters have substantial expressive power even over frozen random features. The authors additionally conclude that their per-feature position matters and that training only these parameters naturally disables a substantial fraction of features.
record.recipe_differences: Only BatchNorm affine parameters are trained while other weights remain frozen at random initialization; reported outcomes are test accuracies, not training classification errors.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with network depth and width; initializing β to 1 increases BatchNorm-only accuracy by 1 to 3 percentage points across tested depths and widths.

fits_no_version.finding: Training only BatchNorm affine parameters over frozen random features yields substantial test accuracy, increasing with depth or width in the reported networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned shifts and rescalings of frozen random CNN features can represent useful image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E reports that alternative frozen-feature initializations have no discernible accuracy effect. Initializing γ and β to 1 improves BatchNorm-only accuracy but causes many fully trainable deep CIFAR-10 ResNet runs to fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effects of BatchNorm affine initialization depend on whether features are frozen or trainable.

record.problems: The study reports test accuracy rather than training error, and only considers ResNets on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet; the authors note they did not search for hyperparameters specific to training only BatchNorm.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible explicit text values for this result were left out; figure-only model values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error under ordinary full-network training, including corrupted labels and model-size or recipe effects.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with plain-network depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization exceptions.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks, signal and gradient propagation, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in deep tanh networks.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence thresholds.
BatchNorm versus no-BatchNorm convergence speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix E concerns residual-network initialization and final accuracy or run failure; it does not establish V4's plain-network learning-speed or trainable-depth effects. Affine-parameter ablations retain normalization and therefore do not test V6. The record's statement that experiments consider only ResNets overlooks the VGG experiments in Appendix C.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 fitting, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, training duration, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Training error as a function of plain-network depth and identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization comparisons.
Initialization effects on learning speed, trainable depth, and training error.
Learning-rate stability, loss trajectories, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Whether BatchNorm speeds accuracy gains or tolerates higher learning rates, and comparisons with Fixup.
